cards.title: EMA crossover had the best risk-adjusted return after costs
cards.body: EMA crossover returned 20.8% a year net of costs with a Sharpe of 1.00 and a worst drawdown of -14.2%. Equal-weight buy-and-hold of the same 44 stocks had a Sharpe of 0.78 (-43.2% drawdown), and the Nifty 50 index 0.24. Only 3 of 14 strategies beat plain buy-and-hold on Sharpe. By family, Stat-arb scored highest on average (0.96) and Machine learning lowest (-0.26).

cards.title: Being right more often did not mean making more money
cards.metric_label: rank correlation, hit rate vs Sharpe
cards.body: Across 484 strategy-stock pairs the link between daily hit rate and net Sharpe is weak (Spearman 0.18). RSI reversal won 70% of its trades but had a Sharpe of 0.30; EMA crossover won only 38% yet reached 1.00, because its average win was 3.5x its average loss (vs 0.8x). Payoff size matters as much as hit rate.

chart.label: Net Sharpe, strategies ordered by win rate (highest first)

cards.title: Costs wiped out Random forest
cards.body: A delivery round trip costs about 0.32% (STT, exchange and SEBI fees, GST, stamp duty, 5 bps slippage a side). Random forest turned its portfolio over 89x a year, so costs took about 14.3% a year and its CAGR fell from 17.1% to 1.4%. Strategies trading less than 5x a year kept on average 96% of their gross CAGR.

cards.title: Most strategies did better in high volatility than in calm markets
cards.metric_label: avg Sharpe, high vs low VIX
cards.body: Averaged across strategies, Sharpe was 0.73 in high-VIX days and -0.17 in low-VIX days. Pairs trading (long-only) led in high volatility (1.45); in bear tags the leader was EMA crossover (1.28) and in bull tags EMA crossover (0.80). The 200-day rule is slow: its longest-rising 'bear' spell (Mar 2020 to Jul 2020) saw the Nifty gain 38%, which is why buying in 'bear' tags looked good.

chart.label: Sharpe in high VIX (bar) vs low VIX (dot)

cards.title: The best in-sample setting never stayed the best
cards.metric_label: parameter grids where the best 2010-19 setting was still #1 after 2020
cards.body: For SMA crossover, the best 2010-2019 setting (fast=100, slow=250, Sharpe 1.10) ranked 14 of 15 after 2020 (Sharpe 0.16); in 2 of 6 grids the in-sample winner fell into the bottom half. 10 of 14 strategies had a lower Sharpe out of sample. After deflating for the 84 configurations tested, no strategy cleared 95% confidence that its Sharpe beats luck.

cards.title: ML models did not beat simple rules once both paid the same costs
cards.body: Walk-forward models (retrained every year on past data only) reached an out-of-sample AUC of 0.507-0.513, barely above a coin flip (0.5). Gross of costs the best ML model, Logistic regression, had a Sharpe of 0.81; net it was 0.06, against 1.00 for EMA crossover. Next-day predictions flip often, so the models trade 60-96x a year.

cards.title: Survivorship bias inflates every stock-level result
cards.metric_label: CAGR: today's constituents vs Nifty index
cards.body: The universe is today's Nifty 50 members with 10+ years of history, chosen with hindsight. Holding them equally from 2010 returned 21.4% a year against 9.4% for the Nifty 50 price index (which excludes about 1-1.5% a year of dividends). Compare strategies with each other and with stock buy-and-hold, not with the index.

cards.title: RSI reversal diversified the rest the most
cards.metric_label: average return correlation with other strategies
cards.body: RSI reversal had the lowest average daily-return correlation with the other strategies (0.48). The least correlated pair was Donchian breakout and RSI reversal (0.13). An equal-weight mix of all rule-based strategies returned 13.3% a year with a Sharpe of 0.75 and a -20.3% worst drawdown.

chart.label: Average correlation with the other strategies (lower diversifies more)

cards.title: Results differ a lot by sector
cards.metric_label: trend-family Sharpe, best vs worst sector
cards.body: Trend strategies worked best in Financial Services (avg Sharpe 0.66) and worst in Oil Gas & Consumable Fuels (-0.05). Mean-reversion strategies did best in Healthcare (0.33) and worst in Oil Gas & Consumable Fuels (0.12). Sector groups hold 3-11 stocks, so treat these as indicative.

chart.label: Avg Sharpe: trend (bar) vs mean reversion (dot)
